signals.signal: 68% of peer banks are live on FedNow while First Capital is not.
signals.implication: Payment modernization is now a commercial-retention and competitive parity issue, not a discretionary technology feature.

signals.signal: First Capital digital adoption is 41% against 67% peer median.
signals.implication: Digital banking gap contributes to branch cost load, customer attrition, and mobile acquisition weakness.

signals.signal: First Capital's 68% cost-to-income ratio is 10 points above peer median and 13 points above board target.
signals.implication: AI bets must be framed around measurable cost-to-income movement, not experimentation.

signals.signal: BSA/AML automation and SAR timeliness are common examiner focus areas as instant payments expand.
signals.implication: FedNow cannot scale without real-time fraud and AML controls.

signals.signal: Regional banks increasingly avoid big-bang core replacement by adding API/payment middleware around legacy cores.
signals.implication: First Capital can sequence API layer first, then decide on full core replacement later.
